text: There's no order book inside a Uniswap-style pool and nobody setting a price. There's one formula — x times y equals k — and every price you see is just a consequence of that formula and the pool's current reserves.

Take a pool holding 100 ETH and 200,000 USDC. Multiply the reserves and you get k, 20 million — the value every trade must keep constant. The spot price is just the ratio of reserves, 2,000 USDC per ETH.

Send 10 ETH into that pool. The new ETH reserve is 110; dividing k by 110 gives roughly 181,818 USDC, so the trader receives about 18,182 USDC — an effective price of 1,818 per ETH, worse than the 2,000 spot price. That gap is price impact.

A 1 ETH trade moves the price about 1 percent. A 50 ETH trade moves it over 33 percent. The curve gets steeper as a reserve depletes, so pool depth, not any setting a team tunes, is what actually determines execution quality.
x times y equals k, and everything else — spot price, price impact, fee accrual — follows from that one invariant. Next up: liquidity pools and the LP tokens that represent your share of them.
